A regular hexagon can be divided into six equilateral triangles by drawing lines from the center to each vertex. Each of these triangles has a side that is also a side of the hexagon, meaning the side length of the hexagon equals the side length of one triangle.

Given the perimeter of one equilateral triangle is 21 inches, and an equilateral triangle has three equal sides:

Side length of triangle = 21 ÷ 3 = 7 inches.

Thus, the side length of the regular hexagon is also 7 inches. A regular hexagon has six equal sides, so its perimeter is:

Perimeter = 6 × 7 = 42 inches.

Answer: 42
